terms.gloss: set (a plant, a cutting) in the ground
evidence: Plin. NH 17.67: hōc modō plantantur Pūnicae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From planta, a cutting or seedling. The classical writers say serere or pōnere.

phrases.latin: quī ūnum phasēlum sēvit et quīnquāgintā lēgit
phrases.english: who planted one bean and picked fifty
Let’s plant some seeds in the little garden.

phrases.latin: Ecce, agricolae orȳzam serunt, singulās plantās in lutum dēfīgentēs.
phrases.english: Look, the farmers are planting rice, pushing each seedling into the mud.

phrases.latin: Cum orȳzam sēvērunt, aquam in agrōs immittunt.
phrases.english: When they have planted the rice, they let the water into the fields.

sources: Lewis & Short: sero · Lewis & Short: planta
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 166.
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
